details.text: `g25` has been full since about Nov 11 22:05. Both nodes were full through the Nov 12 16:08 run.
In the 21:04 run, `g26` held until about 21:30 and `g25` until at least 21:44.
Every MI35x 8-GPU nightly test that landed on these nodes failed in about 2 minutes. Earlier jobs (`g12`, `g13`, `g16`, `g27`) are in yesterday's report.

details.label: Top hypothesis
details.text: `[HIGH]` a GPU workload that the runner pods cannot see holds all 8 GPUs on each node. No change is blamed. The holders are 8 processes per node with about 300 GB each (PIDs 3032968–3032975 in the 16:08 run).

details.label: Disconfirming
details.text: the owner is still unknown. Some analyses describe a live workload (memory and compute counters kept rising on Nov 11); others describe leaked KFD contexts.

details.label: In-flight fix
details.text: ⚠️ [#49956](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49956) (open since Nov 12) makes the preflight fail on bad `rocm-smi` output. It does not free the GPUs. [#49942](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49942) (skip follow-up steps after a failed setup) was closed without merging. ❌ Nothing addresses the nodes themselves.

details.label: Suggested triage
details.text: on both hosts, runner owners run `ps -o pid,ppid,etime,cmd` and `cat /proc/<pid>/cgroup` on the KFD PIDs to find the owner. Take the nodes out of service until they are clean, then re-run the two Nov 12 nightlies.
